summary: ArchiMate models an instance holds, as Archi `.archimate` files (plain XML or Archi's zipped archive), named by `cat-archimate.config.json` (cat-harness's `archimate` subgraph). Every view, element and relationship in a model is a node of its own: a page and an IRI, keyed by Archi's own id, and every view is drawn as SVG from the model's diagram.

avatar.reads: three boxes and the lines between them — an architecture drawn as a model, every box an element

rationale: The `openapi` kind's shape applied to an ArchiMate model (owner, 2026-10-09: "need new specialixed harness (like openapi) for archimate content in the KG"). `content`, not `derived` as `openapi` is: an OpenAPI document is ingested from the API's repository and changed by re-ingesting, but an ArchiMate model is AUTHORED where it is held — smart-ra's are drawn in Archi and committed beside the document they describe — so a QA finding against one is a finding against its authors, which is what `content` says. Not renderable: the site build does not read this directory. Its pages, one per view, element and relationship, are written by the tools layer's `archimate/scripts/gen-archimate-pages.ts`, into the graph (`served: true`, as `openapi` does) or into a site being built (`--out`), since a large model is thousands of nodes. The config's family is validated as a file. A model file carries no `$schema`: it is checked by parsing it (`check-archimate.ts`), and what it is read into is the DERIVED family `archimate-model/v1` (`derived: true`), registered so the UML overview draws Model, Element, Relationship and View from it (owner, 2026-10-31: "i dont really like native UML, rather derived"; smart-ra#166 D2).
